smell_validity.evidence: One retired Python-2 compatibility layer leaves every region provably inert: guards on pinned-False switches, version checks no supported interpreter passes, a true-or-true decision arm, a post-return tail, and helper/switch modules nothing live imports. The canonical switch-off-without-cleanup fault is unmistakable, its cost real (students copy this package as their structural example), while caller-less live functions stay clearly separate from the layer.

maintenance_impact.evidence: A lasting trap, not a local edit: every future change and reader must trace inert guards across nine files, two orphan modules and history comments that misrepresent which interpreters the package supports; re-enabling a switch would silently change exercise outputs. Removal restores the near-empty package roots the lesson demonstrates. Lasting gain, but bounded to one small mock package, not architecture-level.

development_plausibility.evidence: Era-authentic: the _compat.py convention, array/struct/StringIO idioms, guard styles that vary naturally, matching @see docstrings, first-edition alias comments, and a believable simplification tail. The retired functionality is credible and its reason for remaining is the plausible switch retirement. It falls short of indistinguishable-from-evolution only through faint regularity: every package file participates, each with one tidy retained region.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: It materially de-risks wrong direction, incomplete cleanup and redesign scope: it enumerates every retained shape (guarded branches, the unwinnable arm, inlined paths, the leftover tail, helper and switch modules), sets a decidable finished state, pins preservation (mock strings, import styles, untouched tests and lesson texts, package-only scope), and demands a package-wide sweep. Deletion mechanics stay open.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Distinct purposes need distinct code-supported decisions: deleting whole orphan modules (import-graph check), removing import-time guard and alias suites, dissolving an always-true two-arm decision, pruning in-function legacy branches while preserving the mock contract, and stripping an unreachable post-return tail justified by control flow alone. The deletion action repeats; the correctness argument differs at every purpose.

localization_burden.evidence: Guard classification combines the switch module's pinned values with each consumer's condition across files; the prompt locates the package and mandates a roots-and-leaves sweep but names no affected files. Config selection, aliases and the registry load the layer; exclusions needed: reverse and wav functions have zero in-package callers yet stay. No chained second indirect mechanism.

repair_coordination.evidence: One shared rule couples the nine files: retired switches, their imports and the two orphan modules must move together. Deleting either module before cleaning consumers raises ImportError when the lesson test imports the package, subpackages or member modules; cleaning all guards while keeping the modules passes tests yet leaves the layer. No second rule interacts with that coupling.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: Preserved behavior is unchanged mock returns plus the import surface. One uniform rule (delete every region referencing the two helper/switch modules or the three pinned constants, then prune the orphan modules and unused imports) covers all nine regions and both modules; even the post-return tail imports the helper, so the same sweep finds it. No location needs a per-location behavioral decision.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Import-structure mistakes (deleting a live member module, or a switch module before its consumers) fail immediately when the suite imports the package three ways. A subtler over-deletion (removing the live mock return in echo.py) runs and returns a plainly comparable wrong value on any call. No special state or ordering is needed; no hidden untested failure path is established.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
